title: VoiceDesk
tagline: Voice-note inbox with AI agent assist
description: A full-stack voice-note inbox for small Nigerian businesses. Customer voice notes in Pidgin, Yorùbá, Igbo, Hausa or English are transcribed, translated, tagged by intent, and answered with a draft grounded in the business's own approved answers. A human approves every reply before it is sent.
highlights: ~6,100 LOC FastAPI backend and ~6,400 LOC Next.js + TypeScript frontend
166 pytest tests against real Postgres plus 30 Playwright end-to-end tests with axe accessibility checks
Idempotent, resumable 4-step pipeline: transcribe → translate → tag intent → draft reply
Approval gate: sending a reply without an approval record is rejected with HTTP 409
Postgres job queue with SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED instead of Redis
Provider-agnostic STT and LLM adapters (ElevenLabs Scribe v2, any OpenAI-compatible model)
Live inbox updates over Server-Sent Events
Public in-browser recording page (MediaRecorder) and tokenised customer status page
WhatsApp and Telegram channels behind the same pipeline
Owner/agent roles, rotating refresh tokens, workspace isolation on every query
problem: Nigerian customers send voice notes instead of typing, often mixing Pidgin, Yorùbá, Igbo, Hausa and English in one sentence. A small business owner getting 80 voice notes a day can't listen to them all, agents don't speak every language, and generic chatbots built for typed English give wrong answers where money or health is involved.
constraints: A human approves every reply — the AI draft is stored separately from the sent reply
Drafts come only from the business's approved knowledge base; no match means a visible 'needs an agent' flag
Every pipeline step can fail, and failures must be shown, not hidden
Retrying a step must never transcribe, translate or bill twice
Workspaces are isolated, and voice data is handled under NDPA 2023 (consent, retention, no audio in logs)
Be honest about language quality: languages with high word error rate are labelled beta
architecture: Monorepo: api/ (FastAPI, SQLModel, Alembic) and web/ (Next.js Pages Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui)
Upload creates the message and its job row in one Postgres transaction, so no job is ever lost or orphaned
A poll loop inside the API claims jobs safely and runs the pipeline; each step_run is unique on (message_id, step)
STT and LLM vendors sit behind small Protocol interfaces chosen by env var, with fake providers that count calls for tests
An in-process SSE broker pushes status changes to the agent inbox in real time
Next.js API routes keep the rotating refresh token in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie; only the 15-minute access token reaches the browser
Deployed on Vercel (web), Render (API, Docker) and Neon (Postgres), with Cloudinary for audio
decisions: Chose a Postgres job table over Redis — the volume is small, idempotency state lives in the DB anyway, and enqueueing in the same transaction removes a class of bugs
Chose ElevenLabs Scribe v2 over Whisper, which scores above 100% WER on Hausa, Igbo and Yorùbá and has no Pidgin support
Made every step idempotent and resumable so a retry from the UI resumes at the failed step without repeating paid calls
Kept vendors behind adapters so a new STT or LLM provider is one class, with no pipeline changes
Covered cross-boundary flows (browser → Next.js server → API) with Playwright rather than mocking them
next: Run the WER research spike on consented local audio and replace vendor figures
WhatsApp for many businesses via Embedded Signup
Spoken replies in the customer's language (TTS)
Usage-based billing by minutes processed and agent seats
pipelineNote: Each step is keyed by (message_id, step). A failed step retries from where it stopped, so finished steps are never re-called or re-billed. Sending without an approval returns 409.
